successors.name: Canada
successors.text: British Columbia as the united colony of 1866-1871 and the province of 1871: the mainland, Vancouver Island and the Queen Charlotte Islands

ledger.x: 1858: the mainland becomes the Colony of British Columbia.
1859: New Westminster replaces Fort Langley as capital (infobox 'Fort Langley (1858-1859); New Westminster (1859-1866)').
1863: the Stickeen Territories join British Columbia.
1866: Vancouver Island is united with British Columbia.
1866: Victoria becomes the capital of the united colony ('1866-1871: Victoria', infobox).
1866: the San Juan Islands dispute, begun in 1859 under the Colony of Vancouver Island (twelve-year standoff), passes to the united colony; the start is inherited (confidence 1).
1871: the San Juan Islands are 'awarded to the United States following third-party arbitration by the German Empire in 1871' (Pig War page; other sources 1872).
1871: the Colony of British Columbia ends on 20 July 1871.

certainty.note: No boundary survey on the pages; the 49th parallel is the Oregon Treaty line (sharp), the northern limit approximate.
The 60th parallel and the 120th meridian west are named lines; the boundary with the Alaska panhandle was disputed (Stikine Territory page: until the 1903 Alaska Boundary Settlement).
